answer: A new key only earns after it crosses a minimum-cut test on the countersignature graph. Established graders form the core along a published ridge; the node then asks how few bonded edges must be cut to isolate the applicant. If that cut is thinner than three uncorrelated backers, or if several keys share one funding path, the cluster is collapsed to a single seat and the locked quartz is slashed. Survivors stay on a yarrow probation list until two later epochs bring independent panels, so a farm hanging many names off one bridge bleeds stake instead of multiplying votes.
